title: Elastic lane fencing, probe-based throttles, and cooperative eviction for noisy-tenant mitigation
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Define and implement an 'elastic lane fencing' system combined with probe-based throttles and cooperative eviction signals to isolate noisy tenants, enforce throughput guarantees, and limit cross-tenant tail latency impact on Dedicated GPU pools. This ticket captures design, API hooks, scheduler changes, runtime protections, rollout strategy, and observability required to ship a production-ready mitigation layer that works alongside existing quota and preemption controls.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant lane fencing can pin a configurable fraction of GPU lanes and prevent spillover beyond configured burst budgets
Probe-based throttles detect sustained tenant-backed queue growth within 30s and reduce new-ticket admission to a configured rate without blocking healthy tenants
Cooperative eviction signal allows callers to choose best-effort degradation (lower batch sizes, shorter kv-cache retention) within 5s of signal reception
E2E tests simulate 50 concurrent tenants with one noisy tenant and show <10% latency tail degradation for non-noisy tenants compared to baseline
Metrics emitted for throttles, fence hits, cooperative evictions, and denied-admissions are available in Console under runtime-2.3 dashboards
Feature can be toggled per-dedicated-pool and per-tenant via Console and API; default off for existing pools and on for new pools with runtime-2.3 release
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with runtime, scheduler, and console leads. Agreed on three-layer approach (fencing, probe-throttle, cooperative-evict).

2026-03-04: Prototype of lane fencing API sketched; added parameters: min_reserved_lanes, burst_bucket_tokens, refill_rate. Linked design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Elastic+Lane+Fencing+Design

2026-03-07: Benchmarked probe-based admission controller locally with small GPU cluster; identified 2s probe interval as sweet spot for short bursts. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1983
2026-03-09: Compatibility check with existing quota enforcement; decided to make fencing orthogonal to hard quotas and prefer soft preemption when both apply.

2026-03-11: Implemented telemetry events for fence_hit and throttle_engaged; sample metrics names planned: redwood.fence.hits, redwood.throttle.admissions_dropped. Draft dashboard in Console: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/runtime-2.3/fleet-isolation
2026-03-12: Safety review with SRE; added rollback playbook and emergency disable API. Preparing integration test matrix for canary rollout.
decisions: Keep lane fencing soft by default (refill token-bucket) rather than hard exclusive GPU allocation to increase utilization in mixed workloads
Probe-based throttles will use lightweight RTT and queue-depth probes rather than deep sampling to limit overhead
Cooperative eviction exposes a minimal semantic API to model runners: {reduce_batch:true, shorten_kv_ttl:true, degrade_precision:false} so operators and SDKs can opt-in behavior per model
Make fencing and throttles configurable at pool and tenant scope with Console controls rather than only through infra manifests
tradeoffs: Soft fencing increases overall utilization but can allow short-lived bursts to temporarily affect other tenants; mitigated via fast probes and conservative defaults
Probe frequency versus noise: higher probe rates react faster but add scheduling overhead; chosen 2s–5s adaptive window
Cooperative eviction requires model/runner support; some legacy runners will fall back to hard preemption which impacts throughput
Complexity in scheduler increases testing surface and rollout risk; we mitigate by feature flagging and staged canary rollout
rollout_plan: Stage 0 (dev): unit tests and local cluster smoke tests
Stage 1 (canary): enable fencing + probe throttles on 2 dedicated pools with internal tenants only; 2-week observation
Stage 2 (gradual): enable per-tenant UI controls for customers that opt-in; monitor telemetry for 4 weeks
Stage 3 (default opt-in): enable conservative defaults for new pools in runtime-2.3; allow opt-out via pool config
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboard panels: fence.hit_rate, throttle.drop_rate, coop_evict.count, downstream_tail_p99_delta
Alert: throttle.drop_rate > 0.5% sustained for 10m -> page on-call SRE
SLO check: non-noisy-tenant p99 latency increase must be < 10% compared to baseline or trigger rollback
test_plan: Unit tests for token-bucket refill and fence decision logic
Integration test that spins up 50 tenants with one noisy tenant and asserts isolation metrics
Chaos test: simulate controller lag and verify cooperative eviction fallback to hard preemption
Load test: verify throughput guarantees under 80% cluster utilization
